findings.body: `canDelete` becomes true through the new Prometheus ability, but the menu still renders Delete only under `canDelete && rulerRule`, so users cannot delete rules from the updated list view.
findings.failure_mode: The destructive action is silently omitted despite a supported and allowed delete ability.
findings.impact: `canDelete` becomes true through the new Prometheus ability, but the menu still renders Delete only under `canDelete && rulerRule`, so users cannot delete rules from the updated list view.
findings.root_cause: Prometheus-based delete authorization was added without converting the delete menu from its ruler-object dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the delete menu item operate on the already available editable identifier and group identifier, remove the `rulerRule` rendering requirement, and change `handleDelete` so it does not require a `RulerRuleDTO`.
findings.title: Delete disappears for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.trigger: Render a Grafana rule list item from the Prometheus response without a `rulerRule`, while the user has permission to delete the rule.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `canDelete` via Prometheus ability (line 87) but AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 165 still requires `canDelete && rulerRule` to render Delete menu item. When rulerRule is undefined but promRule grants delete ability, Delete won't appear despite canDelete being true.

findings.body: The Prometheus ability can authorize pausing, but the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and passes a ruler DTO to `MenuItemPauseRule`; therefore Pause is never shown on the new list path.
findings.failure_mode: Users lose the pause/unpause action in the list view after ruler data is removed.
findings.impact: The Prometheus ability can authorize pausing, but the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and passes a ruler DTO to `MenuItemPauseRule`; therefore Pause is never shown on the new list path.
findings.root_cause: The permission calculation was migrated to Prometheus data while the pause action implementation remained ruler-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Adapt the pause action to accept the Grafana rule identifier and Prometheus pause state, or lazily obtain the required mutation data when the action is invoked, then remove the ruler-only render guard.
findings.title: Pause disappears for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.trigger: Render an editable Grafana-managed rule using only its `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`, as the new list view now does.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `canPause` via Prometheus ability (line 83) but AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 123 requires `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and passes rulerRule to MenuItemPauseRule. Without rulerRule, Pause won't render despite canPause being true.

findings.body: Update and delete support can be reported for a federated rule even though the previous implementation detected its federated group and marked it immutable, exposing invalid edit and removal actions.
findings.failure_mode: The ability layer advertises mutations that are unsupported for federated rule groups.
findings.impact: Update and delete support can be reported for a federated rule even though the previous implementation detected its federated group and marked it immutable, exposing invalid edit and removal actions.
findings.root_cause: The refactor discarded the `CombinedRule` group information and replaced federated-rule detection with a constant.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the group metadata needed by the ability hook and restore `isFederatedRuleGroup` detection instead of hard-coding `false`.
findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
findings.trigger: Evaluate abilities for a federated Mimir rule through `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` or `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch explicitly sets `const isFederated = false` at line 245 with TODO comment, replacing previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` detection. This allows mutations on federated rules that should be immutable.

findings.body: React emits the missing-key warning and reconciles items by position; local action state such as an open clone confirmation or silence state can be retained for a different rule after the result set changes.
findings.failure_mode: List reconciliation is unstable and can associate child component state with the wrong rule.
findings.impact: React emits the missing-key warning and reconciles items by position; local action state such as an open clone confirmation or silence state can be retained for a different rule after the result set changes.
findings.root_cause: The component replacement dropped the `key` prop from the Grafana branch of the mapped result list.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the existing stable value as `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, matching the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` invocation.
findings.title: Grafana results in FilterView are rendered without React keys
findings.trigger: Render multiple Grafana results and then filter, remove, or reorder them while a stateful rule action component is mounted.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 157 shows `<GrafanaRuleListItem` without key prop, while line 165 shows `<DataSourceRuleLoader key={key}`. The removed GrafanaRuleLoader had `key={key}`. Missing React key causes reconciliation issues.

validated_findings.impact: The Prometheus ability can authorize pausing, but the menu still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and passes a ruler DTO to `MenuItemPauseRule`; therefore Pause is never shown on the new list path.
validated_findings.root_cause: The permission calculation was migrated to Prometheus data while the pause action implementation remained ruler-only.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Adapt the pause action to accept the Grafana rule identifier and Prometheus pause state, or lazily obtain the required mutation data when the action is invoked, then remove the ruler-only render guard.
validated_findings.title: Pause disappears for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
validated_findings.trigger: Render an editable Grafana-managed rule using only its `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`, as the new list view now does.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `canPause` via Prometheus ability (line 83) but AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 123 requires `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and passes rulerRule to MenuItemPauseRule. Without rulerRule, Pause won't render despite canPause being true.

validated_findings.body: The click sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but `RuleActionsButtons` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when its absent `rule` prop is a ruler alerting rule, so no drawer opens and the action visibly does nothing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: An enabled menu item accepts the click without displaying the silence workflow.
validated_findings.impact: The click sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but `RuleActionsButtons` renders `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` only when its absent `rule` prop is a ruler alerting rule, so no drawer opens and the action visibly does nothing.
validated_findings.root_cause: The component is now invoked with only `promRule`, but the silence drawer remains conditionally rendered from the optional ruler rule.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Allow the silence drawer to take the Prometheus rule UID, and gate its rendering using `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)` when no ruler rule is supplied.
validated_findings.title: Silence menu action is a no-op for the new Prometheus-only list item
validated_findings.trigger: Click “Silence notifications” on a Grafana alert rendered by `GrafanaRuleListItem` when the user has silence permission.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons (line 47). RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx line 104 renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` which checks the ruler rule prop, not promRule. Click sets showSilenceDrawer but drawer won't render.

validated_findings.body: Update and delete support can be reported for a federated rule even though the previous implementation detected its federated group and marked it immutable, exposing invalid edit and removal actions.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The ability layer advertises mutations that are unsupported for federated rule groups.
validated_findings.impact: Update and delete support can be reported for a federated rule even though the previous implementation detected its federated group and marked it immutable, exposing invalid edit and removal actions.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor discarded the `CombinedRule` group information and replaced federated-rule detection with a constant.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the group metadata needed by the ability hook and restore `isFederatedRuleGroup` detection instead of hard-coding `false`.
validated_findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
validated_findings.trigger: Evaluate abilities for a federated Mimir rule through `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` or `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch explicitly sets `const isFederated = false` at line 245 with TODO comment, replacing previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` detection. This allows mutations on federated rules that should be immutable.

validated_findings.body: The new Prometheus ability marks ModifyExport unsupported because the rule is recording rather than alerting, whereas the ruler-based implementation supported export for every Grafana-managed rule.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The Export menu item is incorrectly absent for recording rules.
validated_findings.impact: The new Prometheus ability marks ModifyExport unsupported because the rule is recording rather than alerting, whereas the ruler-based implementation supported export for every Grafana-managed rule.
validated_findings.root_cause: An alerting-rule subtype predicate replaced the broader Grafana-managed-rule predicate for export support.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a Grafana-managed-rule predicate for ModifyExport rather than `isAlertingRule`, while retaining the existing export permission check.
validated_findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose the export action
validated_findings.trigger: Open the action menu for a Grafana-managed recording rule while holding the Grafana rule export/read permission.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 324 shows `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` replacing previous `[isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, exportAllowed]`. Recording rules are Grafana-managed but not alerting rules, so export is now unsupported for them.

validated_findings.body: Pause is reported unsupported solely because the rule is a recording rule, despite the shared Grafana Prometheus DTO carrying `isPaused` and the previous ruler ability supporting Grafana recording rules.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Recording-rule pause controls remain unavailable even after the Prometheus-only pause UI is implemented.
validated_findings.impact: Pause is reported unsupported solely because the rule is a recording rule, despite the shared Grafana Prometheus DTO carrying `isPaused` and the previous ruler ability supporting Grafana recording rules.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new ability implementation conflates being Grafana-managed with being an alerting rule.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Gate Pause on the presence of a mutable Grafana-managed Prometheus rule rather than on the alerting subtype.
validated_findings.title: Grafana recording rules are incorrectly marked as not pauseable
validated_findings.trigger: Evaluate Pause ability for an editable, non-provisioned Grafana-managed recording rule represented by `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 325 shows `[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, ...]` replacing previous `&& isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`. Recording rules with isPaused field are now marked unsupported for pause.

validated_findings.body: The link no longer contains the previous `returnTo` value, so navigation cannot restore the user's filtered list URL and instead falls back to the generic destination.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Navigation away from a filtered list loses the user's list context.
validated_findings.impact: The link no longer contains the previous `returnTo` value, so navigation cannot restore the user's filtered list URL and instead falls back to the generic destination.
validated_findings.root_cause: The extracted Prometheus-based list item omitted the return-location parameter when rebuilding the view URL.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore `createReturnTo()` and pass it to `createRelativeUrl` as the `returnTo` query parameter, as the replaced list item did.
validated_findings.title: Rule detail links no longer preserve the current list location
validated_findings.trigger: Open a Grafana rule from a filtered or query-parameterized alert list and then use the rule viewer's return navigation.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 40 shows `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` without returnTo parameter. Previous GrafanaRuleLoader used createReturnTo() for this. Navigation loses list context.

validated_findings.body: React emits the missing-key warning and reconciles items by position; local action state such as an open clone confirmation or silence state can be retained for a different rule after the result set changes.
validated_findings.failure_mode: List reconciliation is unstable and can associate child component state with the wrong rule.
validated_findings.impact: React emits the missing-key warning and reconciles items by position; local action state such as an open clone confirmation or silence state can be retained for a different rule after the result set changes.
validated_findings.root_cause: The component replacement dropped the `key` prop from the Grafana branch of the mapped result list.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the existing stable value as `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, matching the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` invocation.
validated_findings.title: Grafana results in FilterView are rendered without React keys
validated_findings.trigger: Render multiple Grafana results and then filter, remove, or reorder them while a stateful rule action component is mounted.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 157 shows `<GrafanaRuleListItem` without key prop, while line 165 shows `<DataSourceRuleLoader key={key}`. The removed GrafanaRuleLoader had `key={key}`. Missing React key causes reconciliation issues.

validated_findings.body: The test passes even though clicking the newly exposed Silence action has no observable effect, allowing the runtime regression to merge.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The interaction contract is untested, so a no-op action is accepted as working behavior.
validated_findings.impact: The test passes even though clicking the newly exposed Silence action has no observable effect, allowing the runtime regression to merge.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new test stops at checking menu-item presence and does not exercise the action handler introduced by the Prometheus-only path.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Click the Silence menu item and assert that the silence drawer/editor opens for the selected rule UID.
validated_findings.title: The silence test verifies visibility but not that the action opens its workflow
validated_findings.trigger: The silence menu item is rendered for a Prometheus-only Grafana rule but its callback cannot render the ruler-dependent drawer.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test at line 194 only asserts `expect(ui.menuItems.silence().get()).toBeInTheDocument()` without clicking and verifying drawer opens. Given candidate 2's finding that drawer won't render, this test gap allows the regression.

validated_findings.body: The expected count treats the menu without Delete as correct, despite defining a Delete selector and granting deletion permission, so the Prometheus-only deletion regression is not detected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The test suite validates an incorrectly truncated action menu for fully authorized users.
validated_findings.impact: The expected count treats the menu without Delete as correct, despite defining a Delete selector and granting deletion permission, so the Prometheus-only deletion regression is not detected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The rewritten test adjusted its expectation to the reduced menu instead of preserving coverage of the existing delete capability.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly assert that the Delete menu item is present and opens the confirmation modal; update or remove the brittle total-count assertion accordingly.
validated_findings.title: The full-permission menu test codifies omission of Delete
validated_findings.trigger: Run the menu test with both global and folder-level `AlertingRuleDelete` permission granted by its `beforeEach` setup.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test at line 207 expects exactly 4 menu items, but test grants AlertingRuleDelete permission. If Delete should appear (per candidate 0), expecting 4 instead of 5 codifies the regression. However, the test may be intentionally testing Prometheus-only path.
